text.autoconfig.spatialhud.title: Spatial HUD
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.enable: Render the bottom HUD strip as a floating hologram. Press H to open these settings.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.autoSc: Keep the panel at a comfortable apparent size as your Minecraft FOV changes. Uses the same scale approach as Spatial GUI.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.fovBas: The FOV at which no automatic scale adjustment is made.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showPa: Show the subtle translucent background behind the floating HUD.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.onlyDu: Never transform the HUD while another screen is open. This preserves inventories, containers, chat, Mod Menu, and modded GUIs exactly as they are.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.distan: Blocks in front of the player's body. This is the hologram's fixed player-relative location, not a screen-space depth.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.planeW: Physical width of the simulated plane in block-like units. Increase it for a larger captured hotbar and status strip.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.height: Legacy setting retained for old config files. Use Virtual HUD Plane Vertical Offset instead.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.virtua: Blocks right or left of the player's body. Positive X moves the hologram right.
Blocks above or below eye height. The default is about waist height, below the normal forward view.
Extra fixed tilt added to the Face-On Look-Down Pitch. Use 0 for the configured physical plane orientation.
The downward view angle where the plane is rectangular. Looking above or below it rotates the mesh into a trapezoid.
Maximum mesh tilt at the horizon. Higher values make the far edge narrower and the captured HUD more squashed when viewed above its face-on angle.
Yaw of the simulated physical plane. Use small values to angle its left and right edges.
Camera Yaw keeps the hologram directly in front when you look left or right. Its mesh pitch still responds to looking up or down. Player Body retains the earlier body-yaw behavior.
How strongly the legacy World Like camera-space plane trails small head motions. It has no effect for Camera Yaw.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.reveal: Hide the complete Spatial HUD below the screen until you deliberately look down. This is enabled by default.
Degrees downward before the panel begins to enter the view. Positive pitch is looking down.
Degrees downward where the panel is fully visible.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.hidden: Extra GUI pixels below the screen while hidden. Higher values guarantee the panel stays out of view.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.lookDo: Safely foreshorten the HUD like a horizontal floating plane: thin at the horizon and fully face-on only after looking down. This is a 2.5D GUI effect, not a world-rendered plane.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.planeF: Degrees downward where the tilted HUD reaches its full height. Increase this to require looking farther down before it looks face-on.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.planeH: How tall the tilted HUD remains at the horizon, as a percent. Lower values give a stronger edge-on floating-plane effect.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.taperB: Give the backing plate a near/far trapezoid shape as you look down. This safely adds width perspective without capturing or warping vanilla HUD icons.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.planeH: Width of the plate's far (upper) edge near the horizon, as a percent of its near edge. Lower values make the taper stronger.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.projec: Scale each vanilla HUD group by its near/far depth using the same perspective ratio as the backing plate. Enabled by default for the strongest safe 2.5D effect; it does not use a framebuffer or global GUI hook.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.experi: Enable Experimental Captured-Texture Warp (Off by Default)

EXPERIMENTAL: capture the selected gameplay bottom-HUD roots and backing into one private texture, then map every finished icon, bar, glyph, AppleSkin, and Detail Armor pixel through the same projective mesh. Normal screens, chat, minimaps, debug text, and other overlays are never captured. It forces gameplay-only operation and returns to the safe affine renderer if an error occurs.
Optional screen-space bow for the experimental captured strip. 0 is a flat projective plane. This setting has no effect unless Experimental Captured-Texture Warp is enabled.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.sway.@: How much the panel gently trails your look direction. Set to 0 for a perfectly rigid HUD.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.swayRe: Lower values settle faster. This is frame-time based, so it stays smooth above 20 FPS.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.rotate: Add a subtle 2D turn as the panel follows your view.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.preser: Keep AppleSkin and Detail Armor Bars Native

When AppleSkin or Detail Armor Bar Reconstructed is installed, keep its affected health, hunger, air, or armor group in its native layout while looking down. This prevents companion overlays from separating, disappearing, or covering each other. Disable only if you prefer to spatially transform every status bar.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showHo: Show the hotbar and spectator controls on the panel.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showBa: Show the vanilla status bars on the panel.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showXp: Show the XP progress bar and level number on the panel.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showMo: Show mount health when riding an entity.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showHe: Show the selected item name above the panel.
